newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Task force for Bosnia refugees to meet next week.
newsitem.headline: Task force for Bosnia refugees to meet next week.

text.p: A new task force created to try to speed up the return home of displaced Bosnians and the reconstruction of their devastated homeland will meet next week, the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said on Tuesday.

The task force, set up on Monday at a Geneva humanitarian meeting on the refugee crisis in former Yugoslavia, will meet in the Bosnian capital Sarajevo to discuss major problems including housing and the return home of ethnic minorities.
UNHCR spokeswoman Pamela O'Toole said the group, made up of representatives of the refugee agency, the World Bank and European Commission, will draw up a plan on returns by March.

More than a year after the U.S.-brokered Dayton peace accord ended 43 months of war in Bosnia, only 250,000 of the 2.1 million uprooted Bosnians have returned home, despite the right to return being central to the peace treaty.
Most are blocked from returning by the failure of the international community to push separatist leaders, mainly in Serb and Croat areas, to stop ethnic intolerance and harassment.
Germany has taken in 320,000 refugees, more than any other country outside former Yugoslavia.
